# MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 - Calibration checks - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Scope
This maintenance manual covers calibration checks and associated verification activities for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03). The document provides background, required tools, stepwise procedure, acceptance criteria, examples of common findings, and recordkeeping requirements. This is intended for certified maintenance technicians and shift engineers performing routine calibration checks and coil inspections. For full preventive maintenance schedules and detailed component replacement procedures, see MM-P1-L1-IH03. Operational startup and shutdown procedures are covered in SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and rationale
Calibration checks on induction billet heaters ensure consistent heating performance, safe operation, and predictable billet quality. The coil assembly, sensing elements, and control feedback loops are susceptible to drift and mechanical wear from thermal cycling and vibration. Regular verification detects changes before they affect forging quality or cause unplanned downtime. To reduce risk, this document emphasizes verifying sensor linearity, coil condition, and control loop response. The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Adhering to this interval aligns coil condition monitoring with heating duty cycles and minimizes the chance of insulation failure or shorting.

Tools
- Appropriate multimeter and insulation resistance tester rated for the equipment voltage class.
- Portable oscilloscope or control-loop analyzer for verifying waveform shape and timing.
- Contact thermometer or non-contact temperature verification device for spot checks of sensor outputs against expected values.
- Hand tools and insulated handling tools as required by site safety policy.
- Approved lubricant for moving linkages and bearings: CFW-LUB-188.
- Personal protective equipment as required by plant standards.

Procedure
Pre-checks and safety
- Coordinate with operations to establish a safe work window and lockout-tagout condition in accordance with plant safety policies. Verify power is removed and controls are in a verified zero-energy state before accessing the coil or sensing assemblies.
- Confirm necessary documentation is available at the worksite including MM-P1-L1-IH03 and the applicable operating procedures SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05. Review previous calibration records for trends.

Visual and mechanical inspection
- Perform a thorough visual inspection of the coil assembly and surrounding insulation. Look for signs of charring, discoloration, abraded insulation, loose terminations, or evidence of coolant leakage where applicable. Check mechanical fasteners for securement and for signs of galling or fretting.
- Where moving parts are present, apply the approved lubricant CFW-LUB-188 to sliding interfaces per manufacturer guidance. Note: only the specified lubricant part number shall be used to preserve compatibility with insulation and seal materials.

Electrical and sensor verification
- Verify insulation resistance of coil windings to ground per site electrical acceptance guidance. Document readings in the maintenance record and compare to previous entries to detect progressive degradation.
- Using a multimeter and control-loop analyzer, verify that sensor outputs correspond to reference checks. For thermocouples or RTD circuits, confirm continuity and stable resistance values under ambient conditions.
- Capture waveform characteristics with a portable oscilloscope to verify the drive waveform shape and timing relative to control commands. Look for abnormalities such as distorted waveforms or unexpected noise that could indicate power electronics issues.

Calibration checks and control loop response
- Simulate a known sensor stimulus and observe the control system response. Verify that setpoint to sensor reading mapping remains within acceptable tolerance as defined in the referenced documents. If drift is observed, adjust calibration per MM-P1-L1-IH03 calibration adjustment steps.
- Reverify loop stability after any adjustment. Ensure that the controller output responds smoothly and without oscillation when a gradual change in setpoint is commanded via operator interface as described in SOP-P1-L1-03.

Examples of common findings and recommended actions
- Insulation discoloration with elevated resistance to ground: recommend coil cleaning and re-insulation; schedule detailed coil maintenance per MM-P1-L1-IH03.
- Loose terminations with intermittent contacts: tighten or replace affected connectors and recheck measurements; log action and retest.
- Sensor drift exceeding documented tolerance: perform sensor replacement or calibration following MM-P1-L1-IH03 instructions and update calibration tag.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil mechanical integrity confirmed with no visible insulation breach or loose fasteners. Insulation resistance measurements consistent with historical baseline and within acceptable degradation bounds specified in MM-P1-L1-IH03.
- Sensor and control-loop verification show stable and repeatable responses. Waveform characteristics and control outputs free of abnormal distortion or excessive noise when compared to baseline capture maintained in system records.
- Lubricated interfaces show smooth mechanical operation after application of lubricant CFW-LUB-188 and require no immediate corrective maintenance.
- Any corrective actions taken are validated by a repeat set of verification checks and documented in the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration checklist with pre- and post-test readings attached to the work order and filed in the equipment history archive. Include oscilloscope captures and multimeter readings as attachments.
- A summary of coil condition assessed at the coil inspection interval: the coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Record the actual equipment run hours at time of inspection and note any interval deviations in the comment field.
- Lubrication log entries specifying the use of lubricant CFW-LUB-188 and the location serviced.
- References to executed procedures and any corrective work orders raised. Link to MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-03, and SOP-P1-L1-05 in the record entry.

Notes
Follow site quality procedures when updating calibration baselines. Any parameter change outside established acceptance criteria requires engineering approval and update of MM-P1-L1-IH03 documentation as applicable.
